b1-unit-52.52.1 Gap Year Diaries: live from the Pan:
Danny: Welcome to a very special Gap Year Diaries! Bruno and I are in the Pantanal, at a small lodge by a river. It's six in the morning, and we've been awake for an hour.
Bruno: Because at five o'clock we heard something screaming outside our window!
Danny: I was as scared as a rabbit. I thought it was a jaguar.
Bruno: It was a group of howler monkeys. Our guide says they call like that every morning.
Danny: Yesterday we went out on a boat. We saw dozens of caimans lying in the sun, and we watched a family of capybaras swim across the river.
Bruno: And Danny felt something land on his head.
Danny: A huge green insect! I didn't move. I was as quiet as a mouse.
Bruno: My favorite moment was in the afternoon. We heard a strange noise in the trees, and then we saw two blue macaws fly over the boat. Huge birds, and so bright!
Danny: Bruno, tell them about the jaguar.
Bruno: When I was a kid, my uncle brought me here, and I saw a jaguar drinking from the river. I've wanted to see one again for twenty years.
Danny: And last night the guide noticed some fresh tracks near the lodge. So tonight we're going out again.
Bruno: There's a good chance we'll see one.
Danny: Or a slight chance! Either way, we'll tell you next week. And listeners: what's the most amazing animal you've ever seen in the wild?
